title: When the Hollow Wakes Anew
premise: Cyrus Amberdale has spent nine years as a temple scribe erasing herself from every ledger she touches, but the Guild of Impossible Things keeps accounts no one can hide from. When a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date—and her—the guild's masters decide she is an asset to be spent, not a person to be saved. Following the prophecy's trail, Cyrus discovers the 'hollow king' of Vaelmoor is a dead man animated by the crown that devoured him, and that her own bloodline wrote the binding spell now failing. To unbind him, she must choose between exposing the guild's founding lie and letting the last dragon-fire die, taking the city's warmth with it. In the end, Cyrus rewrites the prophecy itself at terrible personal cost—binding the crown to her own name and freeing the king, but ensuring she will never be invisible again.
about_author: Ada Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging debts in a merchant house before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people trapped by paperwork, prophecy, and the families they didn't choose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In the temple scriptorium, Cyrus balances the guild's ledgers of impossible trades—a shadow sold twice, a memory pawned—while dodging her overseer's attention. She finds tonight's date inked in a sealed prophecy book that predates the temple. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the moment invisibility fails.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The prophecy names 'the Amberdale hand' and tonight's hour. Cyrus tries scraping the page clean, but the ink regrows overnight. Her only ally, the disgraced archivist Sef, warns her the guild burns its assets when ledgers turn against them. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Summoned before the guildmasters, Cyrus learns they've known about the prophecy for years and have been waiting for its subject to surface. They offer her debt-forgiveness for one task: verify the hollow king's crown in distant Vaelmoor. Emotional beat: the seduction and insult of being valued only as a tool.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid Forward
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. Sef secretly copies the prophecy pages before Cyrus departs, revealing a second name hidden beneath the first—one matching his own family line. He chooses to follow her without telling her why. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Road Through Ashfall
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On the road to Vaelmoor, Cyrus and Sef pass villages going cold as dragon-fire wanes; a dying hearth-keeper gives Cyrus a coal that never dims. She begins questioning what the guild actually does with the fire it collects. Emotional beat: widening moral horizon; guilt as education.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its King
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Vaelmoor is prosperous but strangely joyless; citizens cannot remember the king's face, only their taxes. Cyrus witnesses the crowned figure preside over court without ever blinking. Emotional beat: uncanny horror; the cost of comfortable lies made visible.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Using her scribe credentials, Cyrus gains access to the royal archive and meets the king, who privately begs her—in a voice like dry paper—to find out what he was before the crown. Emotional beat: pity piercing fear; the monster is a prisoner.

chapters.title: Sef's Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. Sef confesses: his ancestors were the binding-spell's co-authors, sworn to maintain it, and his line has been paying the guild in silence for generations. He believes Cyrus's blood can renew or break the binding. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into shared burden; trust rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: The Founders' Cipher
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Deciphering the founders' marginalia, Cyrus learns the crown doesn't animate the king—it eats him slowly, and the guild harvests the overflow as dragon-fire substitute. The prophecy isn't a warning; it's an invoice. Emotional beat: cold fury at elegant, systemic cruelty.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Guided by the undying coal, Cyrus finds the last dragon chained beneath the guild's original vault, nearly guttered, its fire siphoned to light Vaelmoor. It speaks her family name. Emotional beat: awe and grief; inheritance revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The dragon offers a bargain: free it, and it will burn out the crown—but the city's stolen warmth dies with the chain unless someone willingly takes the binding into their own blood. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit; no clean options.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. Sef argues he should take the binding—his line caused this—but Cyrus realizes the spell requires the hand named in the prophecy: hers. Their argument becomes a raw accounting of everything each has sacrificed. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument; loyalty vs. truth fully collided.

chapters.title: The Guild Arrives
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Guild enforcers reach Vaelmoor, having tracked the undying coal. They offer Cyrus a final deal: renew the binding as written and live richly, or be erased from every record—including memory. Emotional beat: terror of annihilation versus the dignity of being remembered.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. The guild partially executes its threat, striking Sef's name from records; people who loved him look through him. Only Cyrus still remembers, because prophecy-ink protects what it names. Emotional beat: horror of institutional forgetting; resolve hardened by loss.

chapters.title: Reading the Crown
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In the royal archive's deepest shelf, Cyrus reads the crown's true history: it was forged from the first king's broken oath, and it hungers for a willing heir. Every renewal has required a sacrifice the guild concealed. Emotional beat: understanding the mechanism; hope acquiring a shape.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. With Sef and the half-remembering king, Cyrus performs the counter-spell in the vault. It works too well—the crown detaches and, unanchored, begins seeking any open mind in the city. Emotional beat: triumph flipping instantly to crisis.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Doors
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. The crown drifts through Vaelmoor entering the ambitious and the grieving alike; the city tears at itself. Sef holds the palace doors with borrowed fire while Cyrus races to finish the rite. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, the body as barricade.

chapters.title: The Willing Heir
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cornered in the vault, Cyrus understands the final clause: the crown must be bound to a name freely given. She writes her own into the prophecy, accepting visibility, memory, and obligation forever. Emotional beat: the climax of choice—inheritance embraced rather than escaped.

chapters.title: Fire Remembers Its Name
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Bound to Cyrus's name, the crown becomes inert metal; the freed dragon-fire floods back through Vaelmoor's hearths, and the king collapses into a peaceful death, finally himself. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief and warmth arriving together.

chapters.title: Auditing the Guild
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. With the prophecy fulfilled and the dragon as witness, Cyrus and Sef present the guild's true ledgers to the restored council of Vaelmoor. The guildmasters are bound by their own contract-magic to honor every debt they hid. Emotional beat: justice as bookkeeping; satisfaction without gloating.

chapters.title: The Name in the Book
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus returns to the scriptorium, no longer erasing herself. She finds her name glowing in the prophecy's final line—not as a victim, but as author of the next page. Sef, restored to record, stands beside her. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; identity claimed.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Wakes Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Epilogue: years later, Scribe-Master Amberdale trains apprentices to read what ledgers conceal. Beneath the temple, the old dragon sleeps warm and free, and once a year Cyrus visits the plain grave of a king who died human. Emotional beat: earned peace; legacy as chosen work rather than inherited chains.
